claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'Linkage Section, IV-33, X-13' followed by the indented sub-entry 'VALUE clause, VI-49'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'Linkage Section, IV-33, X-13' then '  VALUE clause, VI-49'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: Checked the 300dpi render of page 969 (B-57) against page-969.md. The markdown source holds every entry checked on one line each, in PDF order, with sub-entries indented two spaces under their main entry (e.g. 'Linkage Section, IV-33, X-13' / '  VALUE clause, VI-49'; 'LINAGE-COUNTER' / '  Qualified', '  Special register IV-9'), so entry boundaries and the main/sub hierarchy are present in the transcription text. The claim itself concedes the entry text and page references match. The only difference is markup style (bare indented lines vs '- ' list items on other pages), i.e. how a Markdown renderer would reflow them: a formatting/rendering matter that changes no content of an informative index. Under the rejection rules (formatting-only, no change of meaning) this is not a genuine content discrepancy.
